requirements.heading: ARC-Authentication-Results (AAR)
requirements.text: Because there is only one AAR allowed per ARC Set, the AAR MUST contain the combined authres-payload with all of the authentication results from within the participating ADMD, regardless of how many Authentication-Results header fields are attached to the message.

requirements.heading: ARC-Message-Signature (AMS)
requirements.text: As required for undefined tags (in [RFC6376]), if seen, a version tag MUST be ignored; and

requirements.heading: ARC-Message-Signature (AMS)
requirements.text: AMS header fields SHOULD be attached so that any modifications made by the ADMD are included in the signature of the AMS header field.

requirements.heading: ARC-Message-Signature (AMS)
requirements.text: o Authentication-Results header fields MUST NOT be included in AMS signatures as they are likely to be deleted by downstream ADMDs (per [RFC8601], Section 5).

requirements.heading: ARC-Message-Signature (AMS)
requirements.text: o ARC-related header fields (ARC-Authentication-Results, ARC- Message-Signature, and ARC-Seal) MUST NOT be included in the list of header fields covered by the signature of the AMS header field.

requirements.heading: ARC-Message-Signature (AMS)
requirements.text: To preserve the ability to verify the integrity of a message, the signature of the AMS header field SHOULD include any DKIM-Signature header fields already present in the message.

requirements.heading: ARC-Seal (AS)
requirements.text: Note especially that the DKIM "h" tag is NOT allowed and, if found, MUST result in a cv status of "fail" (for more information, see Section 5.1.1); and

requirements.heading: Instance Tags
requirements.text: Valid ARC Sets MUST have exactly one instance of each ARC header field (AAR, AMS, and AS) for a given instance value and signing algorithm.

requirements.heading: Protocol Actions
requirements.text: With this information, Internet Mail Handlers MAY inform local policy decisions regarding disposition of messages that experience authentication failure due to intermediate processing.

requirements.heading: Sealer Actions
requirements.text: All message modifications (including adding a DKIM-Signature header field(s)) MUST be performed before sealing.

requirements.heading: Marking and Sealing "cv=fail" (Invalid) Chains
requirements.text: In the case of a failed Authenticated Received Chain, the header fields included in the signature scope of the AS header field b= value MUST only include the ARC Set header fields created by the MTA that detected the malformed chain, as if this newest ARC Set was the only set present.

requirements.heading: Broad Ability to Seal
requirements.text: Any Internet Mail Handler MAY seal a message by adding a complete ARC Set, whether or not they have modified or are aware of having modified the message.

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: Each ARC Set MUST contain exactly one each of the three ARC header fields (AAR, AMS, and AS).

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: The instance values of the ARC Sets MUST form a continuous sequence from 1..N with no gaps or repetition.

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: The "cv" value for all ARC-Seal header fields MUST NOT be "fail".

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: For ARC Sets with instance values > 1, the values MUST be "pass".

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: For the ARC Set with instance value = 1, the value MUST be "none".

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: The end result of this validation algorithm SHOULD be included within the Authentication-Results header field for the ADMD.

requirements.heading: Validator Actions
requirements.text: As with a DKIM signature ([RFC6376], Section 6.3) that fails verification, a message with an Authenticated Received Chain with a Chain Validation Status of "fail" MUST be treated the same as a message with no Authenticated Received Chain.

requirements.heading: Responding to ARC Validation Failures during the SMTP
requirements.text: If an ARC Validator determines that the incoming message fails ARC validation, the Validator MAY signal the breakage through the extended SMTP response code 5.7.29 ("ARC validation failure") and the corresponding SMTP basic response code.

requirements.heading: Responding to ARC Validation Failures during the SMTP
requirements.text: Because ARC failures are likely only to be detected in the context of other underlying authentication mechanism failures, Validators MAY use the more general 5.7.26 ("Multiple authentication checks failed") instead of the ARC-specific code.

requirements.heading: Communication of Validation Results
requirements.text: If necessary data is available, the ptypes and properties defined in Section 10.2 SHOULD be recorded in an Authentication-Results header field:

requirements.heading: DMARC Local Policy Overrides
requirements.text: As a matter of local policy, a DMARC processor MAY choose to accept the authentication assessments provided by an Authenticated Received Chain when determining if a message is DMARC compliant.

requirements.heading: DMARC Reporting
requirements.text: When an ARC-enabled handler generates a DMARC report, it MAY indicate the influence of ARC on their local policy decision(s) by adding a reason of "local_policy" with a comment string (per [RFC7489], Appendix C) containing a list of data discovered during ARC validation, which at a minimum includes:
